question: Do small encoder- and decoder-only transformers implement fixed-width decimal addition as a modular carrying circuit, which attention heads, residual features, and MLP neurons perform each step, does that mechanism survive changes in depth and length, and is there causal evidence that related circuitry exists in pretrained 7B language models?

key_findings.claim: The controlled task is exhaustive fixed-width interpolation, not unrestricted arithmetic or length generalization.
key_findings.evidence: Inputs enumerate every ordered pair of nonnegative integers a,b with a+b<10^n, pad both operands and the answer to n digits, and encode a+b followed by n equals tokens; for n=3 this gives 500,500 possible pairs. The headline setup randomly trains on 30% and tests on a disjoint 30%, leaving the remaining 40% unused. Fixed positions, leading zeros, excluded overflow, and a random same-distribution split make the task substantially easier than variable-width generation or extrapolation.

key_findings.claim: A one-layer model develops an abrupt attention/QK organization and weight-norm rebound while remaining imperfect, but the paper does not establish a new kind of phase transition.
key_findings.evidence: Across the highlighted one-layer runs, loss falls and accuracy rises while the squared weight norm first decreases and then rebounds; a staircase-like QK pattern emerges abruptly near the rebound. The authors distinguish this from grokking because the change occurs before complete generalization. Six visual runs and descriptive curves do not supply an operational change point, null distribution, intervention, or comparison to prior induction-head and grokking transitions, so 'novel non-grokking phase transition' is stronger than the evidence.

key_findings.claim: The most convincing result is a reproducible two-layer division of labor: first-layer routing forms local digit sums, a second-layer decision head moves previous-position information, and the final MLP applies a carry correction.
key_findings.evidence: In six principal two-layer runs, first-layer heads connect same-significance operand digits and the residual stream separates direct sums below versus at least ten. A second-layer head attends from an output position to the preceding significance position, after which examples separate by whether a carried one is required. Zeroing the final MLP leaves non-carry cases largely correct while turning carry cases into outputs that are often exactly one too small; manually adding one restores those cases. This triangulation is useful, although it does not prove that the decomposition is unique or fully faithful.

key_findings.claim: The corrected plus-or-minus-one metric is a targeted diagnostic rather than an independent proof of the hypothesized carry circuit.
key_findings.evidence: After decision-head or final-MLP ablation, the paper recomputes accuracy after adding or subtracting one from predictions. The recovery is consistent with a missing or spurious carry, but the correction is chosen after positing that exact error class and reports neither full output distributions nor logits, calibration, activation patching, or a reconstructed circuit. It can therefore make a hypothesis-matched off-manifold intervention look more specific than it is.

anchors.section: 5 A closer look at the final MLP

key_findings.claim: The claimed precise neuron localization actually selects a broad task-conditioned majority of the final MLP, not a sparse dedicated subcircuit.
key_findings.evidence: The main 128-wide run assigns about 86 neurons to the carry-relevant set; other configurations use roughly 64/128, 282/512, 650/1024, 94/128 for four digits, and 92/128 in the decoder. Selection is based on post-hoc activation/weight directions and the known task labels. Ablating the selected set creates the predicted carry error, but retaining or removing half to three quarters of an MLP does not justify language about precisely identified dedicated neurons without necessity, sufficiency, resampling, or cross-seed alignment tests.

anchors.section: 5 A closer look at the final MLP

key_findings.claim: The residual-space plots called PCA are correlational, post-hoc, and in the released code are computed with centering disabled.
key_findings.evidence: The manuscript colors the two displayed low-rank directions by carry classes or target digits and sometimes turns to a subleading direction when the leading direction does not match the desired interpretation. It reports no explained variance, held-out probe, quantitative class separation, preregistered direction, or causal intervention. The repository calls torch.pca_lowrank(..., center=False), making the computation an uncentered low-rank SVD whose leading axis may reflect the activation mean rather than variance about the mean; the paper does not disclose that distinction.

key_findings.claim: Changing depth and architecture preserves a broad motif but not a universal one-part-per-step implementation.
key_findings.evidence: Three-layer models still form local sums and eventually apply carry corrections, yet the decision operation can be distributed across multiple heads and layers; one hyperparameter run moves important decision behavior earlier. The two-layer decoder-only model shows staircase routing and carry-sensitive MLP ablations, but uses a different autoregressive layout. These variants support a recurring computational motif, not the stronger claim that each algorithmic step is always assigned to one particular component.

anchors.section: D More details on generative models

key_findings.claim: The four-digit experiment is a useful qualitative extension but is one expensive run rather than a replicated scaling result.
key_findings.evidence: A four-digit model is trained on a roughly 50-million-example exhaustive dataset and reportedly reaches perfect test accuracy. Its attention and residual plots resemble the three-digit circuit, and ablating the final MLP breaks all carry-required positions while manual plus-one correction restores them. The appendix reports one run, no seed sweep or uncertainty, and inconsistent task counts: it enumerates 13 carry classes while Figure 19 says 11 tasks without explaining the reduction.

key_findings.claim: An enlarged-context model trained only on three-digit sums does not learn a length-invariant addition algorithm.
key_findings.evidence: Zero-shot six-digit exact accuracy is only about 10%-15% in the main summary. In the appendix run, it peaks around 0.20 near epoch 500 and falls to about 0.02 by epoch 1000 as out-of-distribution staircase attention and residual separation deteriorate, even while in-distribution positions improve. The negative result is central: an internally human-legible fixed-position motif is not sufficient for length extrapolation.

key_findings.claim: One hundred six-digit priming examples produce high six-digit accuracy, but by a redistributed mechanism that contradicts a clean claim that the original implementation generalizes.
key_findings.evidence: Adding 100 six-digit examples to 150,150 three-digit examples yields 0.93 six-digit exact accuracy after 1,000 epochs and cleaner length-six staircases. However, final-MLP ablation no longer isolates carried-one addition: the MLP primarily corrects non-carry sums and carry work is scattered across head 0:0, head 1:1, and the MLP. A decoder primed with 500 examples reaches only 0.59 and harms three-digit performance. The behavior generalizes better than the advertised modular allocation does.

key_findings.claim: Fine-tuning 500 six-digit examples is effective in one run, but a 0.2% global weight-norm change does not show that the circuit stayed the same.
key_findings.evidence: Starting from the epoch-500 unprimed checkpoint and fine-tuning for 50 epochs on 500 six-digit sums reportedly gives 0.94 six-digit and 0.97 three-digit accuracy. The global norm changes from roughly 481 to 482, and attention/residual plots look similar. Small functionally decisive parameter changes can be hidden in a global norm, and no parameter localization, activation matching, causal circuit comparison, seed sweep, or untouched long-length test supports mechanism preservation.

key_findings.claim: The pretrained-LLM experiment finds arithmetic-correlated heads in three 7B models, but its evidence is explicitly suggestive and methodologically circular.
key_findings.evidence: On 1,000 seeded four-digit prompts, reported exact accuracies are 0.33 for Alpaca-7B, 0.87 for Llemma-7B, and 0.85 for Zephyr-7B. The authors count 164, 190, and 239 heads with full or partial staircases, select eight high-count heads, then try pairs whose ablation lowers accuracy to about 0.17, 0.30, and 0.34-0.35. Discovery, ranking, pair search, and evaluation use the same generated set; there is no held-out head selection, multiple-comparison control, prompt/tokenizer/model-revision robustness, non-arithmetic control, sufficiency test, or complete causal circuit.

key_findings.claim: The reported fraction of LLM errors involving carries is not normalized by how often carry cases occur.
key_findings.evidence: For Llemma and Zephyr, 64% and 74% of mistakes are categorized as carrying mistakes and interpreted as evidence of shared carry structure. Without the carry-case base rate, conditional error rates for carry versus non-carry questions, digit-position controls, or uncertainty, those fractions cannot distinguish a carry-specific weakness from the task distribution. Alpaca response labeling is additionally acknowledged in the release as partly arbitrary.

key_findings.claim: Calling the learned behavior an algorithm needs a narrow qualification that the paper itself partly concedes.
key_findings.evidence: The study infers a compact human-readable fixed-position circuit from attention, class-colored low-rank plots, and zero ablations, while a footnote says 'algorithm' is not meant in a strict sense. It does not test symbol relabeling, base change, digit order, padding, operand permutation, overflow, adversarial long carry chains, or variable length, and zero-shot length transfer fails. The defensible object is a recurring fixed-format circuit or algorithmic motif, not a demonstrated abstract decimal-addition algorithm.

key_findings.claim: Zeroing whole heads, MLPs, or neuron subsets is useful necessity evidence but remains an off-manifold intervention with no robustness or faithfulness audit.
key_findings.evidence: The central causal tests replace component outputs by zero and measure exact or corrected accuracy. The paper does not compare mean, resample, noise, or interchange ablations; patch clean activations; test circuit sufficiency; quantify indirect effects; or reconstruct logits from the proposed circuit. Consequently, ablation failures can reflect distribution shift or interface damage, and surviving behavior can be redundantly implemented.

key_findings.claim: Several visual captions and citations contain material internal inconsistencies.
key_findings.evidence: The four-digit appendix enumerates 13 carry classes, but Figure 19 says its rows are colored by 11 tasks without identifying omissions or merges. Figure 21 defines trinary label 1 as a direct sum at least ten, whereas Figures 23 and 25 say greater than ten, leaving exactly ten unclassified. Appendix A.4 cites Zephyr with reference [6], which is Llemma rather than Zephyr [12]. These appear to be reporting errors, but they make exact replication of the plotted strata ambiguous.

key_findings.claim: The public release offers broad figure-level artifacts but is not a pinned, portable, end-to-end reproduction.
key_findings.evidence: The manuscript-official CarryingTransformers repository at commit 977cc016e36fce067d1b82ef2e269ebddce6324d contains roughly 297 MB across 301 tracked files, including ten Python scripts, six notebooks, checkpoints, data files, and 130 PDFs. Its README maps artifacts to Figures 2-4, 7-17, and 20-25 and Tables 1 and 3-5, while saying Figure 5 checkpoints, the four-digit dataset, and Alpaca raw data are not provided. It has nine commits but no release/tag, license, tests, CI, requirements, environment lock, or paper-pinned snapshot; current HEAD postdates arXiv v2 by 13 days and adds decoder helpers absent from the contemporaneous tree. All ten Python files parse and all six notebooks are valid JSON, but expensive GPU execution was not attempted.

key_findings.claim: The released implementation materially under-specifies and departs from standard RoPE while making the main encoder split nondeterministic.
key_findings.evidence: Training code concatenates q, k, and v and applies the rotary transform to all three, whereas standard RoPE/RoFormer rotates queries and keys rather than values; the paper only says it uses RoFormer positional embeddings. Worse, after distributed initialization each encoder rank entropy-seeds Python independently, creates a different shuffled train/test corpus, and then applies DistributedSampler, so ranks need not train on shards of one dataset and can overlap each other's train/test examples. The length script also uses unseeded long-example generation and two unseeded shuffles. The feed-forward module computes dropout twice, storing an out_p realization that can differ from the returned realization during training. These are architectural and experimental defects, not merely missing documentation.

key_findings.claim: The released length-generalization and figure-reproduction paths cannot execute or regenerate the claimed results without repair.
key_findings.evidence: Length generalisation/Addition_generalisation.py defines args.n_digits and args.n_digits_gen but accesses nonexistent args.n_digit before W&B/training, guaranteeing AttributeError. The only length trainer always initializes a new model and hard-codes 100 priming examples; no code loads the epoch-500 checkpoint and performs the reported 500-example, 50-epoch fine-tune. The current encoder trainer saves a {model, optimizer} checkpoint and seven-item DATA list without attention matrices, while shipped notebooks/checkpoints expect a raw state dict and eight-item payload with epochwise attention. The Figure 2 notebook also plots epoch 300 for a caption that says 400. Thus shipped legacy artifacts support inspection, but current source is not a source-to-results reproduction for Figures 2 or 20-25.

key_findings.claim: Decoder and 7B scripts contain additional likely execution failures and do not specify exact model artifacts.
key_findings.evidence: The decoder trainer creates its causal mask on CPU but applies it to CUDA attention logits, has every distributed rank call os.mkdir on the same output directory before process-group initialization, and lets all ranks initialize W&B and write common paths. The Alpaca script imports an absent train module, hard-codes tokenizer IDs, combines device_map='auto' with model.cuda(), and can crash when a generation contains no integer; Llemma and Zephyr provide result tensors/PDFs but no extraction scripts or exact Hugging Face revisions. These defects sharply narrow the release's reproducibility value.

anchors.section: D More details on generative models

key_findings.claim: The arXiv source is internally complete enough to rebuild the manuscript, but not to regenerate its scientific graphics.
key_findings.evidence: The official v2 source bundle is 37,411,840 bytes with SHA-256 22697527cc69776bb42d7c58dd4e6b024cdfa4bcb93a850244f7b756e3f82fec. It contains 49 files, including the TEX/BIB/BBL/BST and 44 one-page PDF graphics; 29 assets are used by 29 includegraphics calls and 15 are unused revision plots. All 26 figure environments, five tables, references, citations, and graphic targets resolve. A clean TeX Live 2025 build produces 41 pages with normalized text similarity 0.998799 to the official PDF, but source supplies no raw plot data or plotting scripts.

key_findings.claim: The full-adder analogy is explanatory but not an exact circuit equivalence.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix maps the first transformer layer to one half-adder, the second attention block to carry transfer, and the final MLP to an XOR-like correction. A hardware full adder is a binary truth-table circuit, while the model operates over decimal tokens, distributed vectors, approximate attention, and task-conditioned ablations. No truth-table equivalence, Boolean extraction, or verified circuit compilation is shown, so the analogy should not be read as a formal implementation proof.

key_findings.claim: Priority is moderate and narrow: the paper extends prior addition-circuit work with a two-layer carry allocation, but does not originate arithmetic transformers, mechanistic arithmetic analysis, length-generalization study, or phase-transition analysis.
key_findings.evidence: Strict predecessors already study arithmetic limitations, grokking circuits, causal arithmetic mediation, positional encodings, length extrapolation, and exact one-layer n-digit addition; arXiv:2310.13121 is the closest direct predecessor and is cited. The distinctive contribution is the two-layer attention/MLP carry decomposition, its corrected ablations, variants across depth and decoder layout, length priming analysis, and a tentative bridge to three 7B models. Later arXiv:2402.02619 analyzes 49 addition/subtraction models with stronger causal detail, while later length-generalization and pretrained-LLM work substantially broadens or challenges the claims.

method.core_idea: Train tiny transformers on exhaustive fixed-width decimal addition, decompose examples into analytically defined carry classes, and infer a component-level implementation by combining attention geometry, residual low-rank structure, zero ablations, and corrected plus-or-minus-one accuracy.
method.mechanism: For encoder models, the input contains two zero-padded operands and repeated equals placeholders. A first attention layer routes equal-significance digits together so residual states encode direct sums and threshold information. In the canonical two-layer runs, one second-layer decision head moves previous-position sum information to the current output position; the final MLP then changes the direct digit result by one when a carry is required. The analysis labels five principal three-digit carry cases, visualizes class-colored low-rank residual projections, selects MLP neuron subsets by activation/weight directions, and zeros components to test necessity. It repeats variants across width, depth, decoder layout, four digits, six-digit priming/fine-tuning, and three fine-tuned 7B language models.
assumptions: Random held-out examples from the same fixed-width exhaustive space reveal algorithmic computation rather than interpolation shortcuts.

Zero padding, fixed token positions, repeated equals placeholders, most-significant-first ordering, and excluded overflow do not determine the learned solution in a way that undermines abstraction claims.
The five analyst-defined carry classes adequately summarize the important three-digit behavior.
Attention location identifies the information actually carried in head values and used downstream.
A class-colored two-dimensional residual projection identifies a mechanistically used feature rather than a correlated readout.
Uncentered low-rank directions are appropriately described and interpreted as principal components.
Zero ablation creates a meaningful counterfactual rather than an off-distribution residual state.
Recovery after adding or subtracting one uniquely identifies a missing or spurious carry operation.
Large neuron subsets selected using task labels constitute precise localization of a dedicated function.
Similar qualitative plots across six small-model runs establish robustness across initialization and hyperparameters.
The same human decomposition is preferable to alternative learned algorithms or mixed strategies.
A component's necessity establishes the proposed circuit's sufficiency and faithfulness.
A recurring fixed-position motif merits the term algorithm despite failed zero-shot length transfer.
A small priming set reveals generalization of the original implementation even when component roles are redistributed.
A small global parameter-norm change implies mechanistic continuity under fine-tuning.
Staircase-looking heads found and ablated on the same 1,000 prompts are not a multiple-search artifact.
Carry-error fractions are informative without conditioning on the carry-case base rate.
Hard-coded tokenizer IDs and one prompt template represent each named 7B model robustly.
A nonstandard rotary transform applied to values as well as queries and keys does not materially change comparison to standard RoFormer/RoPE models.
Qualitative agreement among three 7B fine-tunes supports extrapolation from the toy circuit to pretrained language models.

techniques.role: Enumerates all fixed-width non-overflow decimal additions with zero padding.
Stratifies examples by direct carry, propagated carry, and non-carry configurations.
Uses one- to three-layer pre-LN encoder transformers with two heads.
Tests a decoder-only autoregressive variant with a related addition layout.
Supplies positional information using a custom RoFormer-like rotary transform.
Visualizes staircase routing between equal-significance digits and output positions.
Identifies heads that move previous-position sum information to the current position.
Zeros head, MLP, or selected-neuron outputs to test component necessity.
Recomputes ablation accuracy after manually adding or subtracting one.
Plots two uncentered low-rank residual directions colored by task or target.
Partitions final-MLP neurons using pre-activation/weight directions and task labels.
Tracks squared weight norm alongside train/test loss and accuracy.
Adds 100 or 500 longer examples to a fixed-width training set.
Fine-tunes an unprimed checkpoint on 500 six-digit examples.
Searches 7B-model attention heads for full or partial staircase patterns.
Ablates selected pairs of high-count arithmetic-correlated LLM heads.
Uses attention, learning-curve, residual-projection, and circuit figures as qualitative diagnostics.

evaluations.setting: One-layer encoder models on random fixed-width three-digit train/test subsets.
evaluations.metric: Train/test loss, exact accuracy, squared weight norm, and attention/QK geometry across epochs.
evaluations.result: The highlighted runs show abrupt staircase formation and a norm rebound but remain imperfect.
evaluations.baseline: Earlier epochs and six initializations; no symbolic or non-transformer baseline.

evaluations.setting: Six two-layer 128-wide encoder runs, principally split 0.3 and weight decay 0.2.
evaluations.metric: Exact and plus/minus-one-corrected accuracy in five carry classes after head or final-MLP zero ablation.
evaluations.result: Decision-head and final-MLP interventions produce class-specific off-by-one failures consistent with carry transfer and carry addition.
evaluations.baseline: Unablated accuracy and alternate heads/components in the same model.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer residual states across positions and carry classes.
evaluations.metric: Two leading uncentered low-rank directions after attention and MLP blocks.
evaluations.result: First-layer plots separate direct sums around ten; second-layer plots often separate carry-required from non-carry cases.
evaluations.baseline: Different layers, positions, and human class labels; no held-out or causal probe.

evaluations.setting: Final MLPs at widths 128, 512, and 1024 and across splits/weight decay.
evaluations.metric: Carry/non-carry accuracy after ablating post-hoc selected neuron subsets.
evaluations.result: Large selected sets reproduce much of the whole-MLP carry error across reported variants.
evaluations.baseline: Complement neuron set and whole final-MLP ablation.

evaluations.setting: Three-layer encoder and two-layer decoder-only variants.
evaluations.metric: Attention maps, residual projections, and carry-stratified ablation accuracy.
evaluations.result: A related motif recurs, but decision behavior is distributed across layers/heads and exact component allocation changes.

evaluations.setting: One four-digit encoder run on an approximately 50-million-example exhaustive dataset.
evaluations.metric: Test accuracy, 13 carry configurations, attention maps, residual projections, and final-MLP ablation.
evaluations.result: Perfect accuracy is claimed and qualitative carry structure recurs; all carry positions fail under final-MLP ablation and recover after adding one.
evaluations.baseline: Three-digit model and non-carry cases; no four-digit seed sweep.

evaluations.setting: Three-digit-trained encoder with a six-digit context and no long examples.
evaluations.metric: Six-digit per-position and exact accuracy across 1,000 epochs plus OOD attention/residual structure.
evaluations.result: Exact accuracy peaks near 0.20 around epoch 500 then falls near 0.02; OOD staircase structure deteriorates.
evaluations.baseline: Three-digit in-distribution positions and epochs before the OOD decline.

evaluations.setting: Three-to-six-digit encoder primed with 100 six-digit examples.
evaluations.metric: Six-digit exact accuracy and internal attention/residual/ablation structure.
evaluations.result: Exact accuracy reaches 0.93, but carry computation is redistributed and the final MLP no longer simply adds the carry.

evaluations.setting: Three-to-six-digit decoder primed with 500 longer examples.
evaluations.result: Six-digit accuracy reaches only 0.59 and original-width performance is harmed.
evaluations.baseline: Unprimed decoder and encoder priming result.

evaluations.setting: Epoch-500 unprimed encoder fine-tuned for 50 epochs on 500 six-digit sums.
evaluations.metric: Six-digit and three-digit exact accuracy, global weight norm, and qualitative internals.
evaluations.result: Accuracy reaches 0.94 and 0.97 respectively while the reported global norm changes about 0.2%.

evaluations.setting: Alpaca-7B, Llemma-7B, and Zephyr-7B on 1,000 seeded four-digit prompts.
evaluations.metric: Exact accuracy, count of full/partial staircase heads, and accuracy after selected two-head ablations.
evaluations.result: Accuracy is 0.33/0.87/0.85; 164/190/239 heads match at least partial patterns; chosen pair ablations reduce accuracy to about 0.17/0.30/0.34-0.35.
evaluations.baseline: Unablated model and other visually counted heads; no held-out selection or prompt controls.

evaluations.setting: All 41 manuscript pages and 26 numbered figures plus five tables.
evaluations.metric: Page-level text/visual consistency, caption definitions, task counts, and claim-to-figure support.
evaluations.result: Every page and numbered visual was inspected; the main qualitative plots are legible, with task-count, inequality, and citation inconsistencies documented.
evaluations.baseline: A caption-consistent, quantitatively specified visual record.

evaluations.metric: Paper coverage, static syntax, dependency pinning, tests, data/checkpoint availability, and code/manuscript consistency.
evaluations.result: All Python parses and notebooks are valid JSON; many artifacts are present, but there is no portable environment or test harness, some headline assets are omitted, and code reveals uncentered projections, nondeterministic shuffles, and nonstandard value rotation.
evaluations.baseline: A tagged, licensed, seeded, dependency-locked, end-to-end reproduction of every final-paper result.

limitations: Author-stated: one-layer models do not reach perfect accuracy and their detailed mechanism remains less clear than the two-layer case.
Author-stated: evidence in Alpaca, Llemma, and Zephyr is suggestive rather than a complete mechanistic explanation.
Author-stated: zero-shot length generalization is poor and worsens late in training.
Author-stated: decoder-only priming is much less effective and can hurt in-distribution performance.
Author-stated: the primed carry operation is scattered through the network rather than cleanly localized to the final MLP.
Reviewer-identified: fixed width, zero padding, fixed positions, repeated equals tokens, most-significant-first ordering, and no overflow permit position-specific shortcuts.
Reviewer-identified: the random held-out set is interpolation within the same exhaustive combinatorial grammar and does not test semantic or algorithmic abstraction.
Reviewer-identified: 40% of the exhaustive three-digit dataset is discarded by the released 30%/30% split.

Reviewer-identified: each distributed encoder rank independently entropy-shuffles and splits the corpus before applying DistributedSampler, so ranks need not share one training set and train/test examples can overlap across ranks.
Reviewer-identified: six primary seeds are too few for a universality claim, and several important extensions use only one reported run.
Reviewer-identified: zero ablation is off-manifold and is not checked against mean, resample, noise, or activation-patching alternatives.
Reviewer-identified: no circuit sufficiency, reconstruction, completeness, or faithfulness metric excludes alternative or redundant mechanisms.
Reviewer-identified: corrected plus/minus-one accuracy is designed around the proposed carry error and is not an independent diagnostic.
Reviewer-identified: neuron localization selects roughly half to three quarters of the MLP and is post-hoc/task-conditioned.
Reviewer-identified: residual plots omit explained variance, quantitative cluster metrics, held-out probes, and causal use tests.
Reviewer-identified: released projections are uncentered although the manuscript repeatedly calls them PCA.
Reviewer-identified: the phase transition has no operational definition, statistical change-point analysis, or priority comparison to induction-head transitions.
Reviewer-identified: the squashing ratio lacks a precise overlap equation, uncertainty, and robustness analysis.
Reviewer-identified: no base change, symbol permutation, digit-order change, padding intervention, operand swap, overflow, or adversarial carry-chain suite tests abstract addition.
Reviewer-identified: priming and fine-tuning results lack seed sweeps, sample-efficiency curves, and independent longer-width validation.
Reviewer-identified: a 0.2% global weight-norm change does not establish circuit preservation under fine-tuning.
Reviewer-identified: LLM head selection and pair ablation are performed post hoc on the same 1,000 prompts.
Reviewer-identified: hundreds of partial-pattern heads, no multiple-comparison correction, and no sufficiency test make LLM localization underdetermined.
Reviewer-identified: LLM carry-error fractions are not normalized by the frequency of carry questions.
Reviewer-identified: only three older fine-tuned 7B models, one prompt format, one tokenizer/revision path, and one generated set are tested.
Reviewer-identified: response cleanup and hard-coded tokenizer IDs make the LLM evaluation fragile; Alpaca labels are partly arbitrary according to the release.
Reviewer-identified: the custom rotary implementation rotates values in addition to queries and keys, a material architectural detail absent from the paper.
Reviewer-identified: the release lacks a license, tests, CI, requirements/environment lock, tags, releases, raw Alpaca data, Figure 5 checkpoints, and the four-digit dataset.
Reviewer-identified: the length-generalization trainer deterministically crashes on a nonexistent args.n_digit attribute before training.
Reviewer-identified: the reported 500-example fine-tuning procedure has no training implementation in the release.
Reviewer-identified: current encoder output formats are incompatible with the shipped checkpoints and notebook analysis payloads.
Reviewer-identified: the Figure 2 notebook uses epoch 300 where the manuscript caption says epoch 400.
Reviewer-identified: the decoder trainer likely applies a CPU causal mask to CUDA logits and has racy multi-rank directory, W&B, and checkpoint writes.
Reviewer-identified: the Alpaca script depends on an absent train module, and Llemma/Zephyr lack extraction code and pinned model revisions.
Reviewer-identified: no training-cost, hardware variance, or memory analysis supports the practical scalability of exhaustive four-digit and longer datasets.
Reviewer-identified: Figure 19's 11-task caption conflicts with 13 enumerated four-digit classes, and Figures 23/25 conflict with Figure 21 at direct sum exactly ten.
failure_modes: A model can attain high random held-out fixed-width accuracy using position-specific circuitry that fails immediately at unseen positions.
Late training can improve in-distribution structure while destroying out-of-distribution staircase attention and exact long-width accuracy.
Zeroing an entire residual contribution can cause interface shift that resembles causal necessity.
Adding or subtracting one can mask wider output-distribution damage when the evaluator only checks corrected exact accuracy.
A broad neuron set can appear function-specific because the selection rule uses the same task labels later used for evaluation.
Uncentered low-rank projections can be dominated by mean activation and still produce visually compelling class separation.
Choosing whichever principal direction best separates labels after inspection can overstate latent modularity.
A decision function can migrate across heads or layers under small hyperparameter changes, defeating one-to-one component narratives.
Priming can improve behavior while replacing the original clean module allocation with a more distributed computation.
Decoder priming can trade long-width gains for degradation at the trained width.
Global parameter norms can barely change while a small consequential circuit is rewritten.
Post-hoc scanning of hundreds of LLM heads will find partial staircase-like patterns by chance or task correlation.
Hard-coded tokenizer token IDs can silently point to different symbols under another model revision or tokenizer.
A generated response with no parsable integer or extra integers can break or mislabel exact-answer evaluation.
Unseeded Python shuffling can make train/test composition and run-to-run claims irreproducible.
Independent per-rank corpus shuffles can create cross-rank train/test leakage and invalidate distributed optimization semantics.
Rotating value vectors can entangle positional phase with content in ways not predicted by standard RoPE analyses.
Exhaustive nested-loop dataset generation scales quadratically in the integer range and becomes impractical beyond small widths.
A human full-adder analogy can obscure decimal, distributed, approximate, or heuristic computations that are behaviorally equivalent in-distribution.
Carry-chain cases near excluded overflow or unseen lengths may fail despite high mean accuracy on the selected five classes.
Caption definition drift can cause an analyst to label the exactly-ten boundary inconsistently across experiments.
reusable_insights: Separate local digit addition, carry detection, carry routing, and carry application when designing arithmetic interpretability probes.
Use answer-correction transforms such as plus/minus one as diagnostics, but validate them against full logits and hypothesis-independent interventions.
Stratify arithmetic evaluations by direct carry, propagated carry, carry-chain length, overflow, and boundary sum exactly nine or ten.
Treat clean fixed-width circuits as hypotheses about abstraction, then test new positions, bases, symbols, formats, and digit orders.
A circuit can be human-readable yet fail to length-generalize; behavioral abstraction and mechanistic legibility are separate axes.
Track out-of-distribution circuit geometry during training because late optimization can selectively erode unseen-position structure.
Small amounts of longer-format data can stabilize positional routing, but the learned mechanism should be re-audited rather than assumed unchanged.
Compare encoder and decoder layouts to distinguish task logic from sequence-format artifacts.
Use activation patching, resample ablation, causal scrubbing, and circuit reconstruction alongside zero ablation.
Report necessity, sufficiency, completeness, and faithfulness separately for any proposed circuit.
Center activations for standard PCA, disclose centering, report explained variance, and evaluate class geometry on held-out data.
Quantify neuron-set sparsity and stability across seeds before describing a localized functional module.
Measure carry-specific error conditional on class frequency rather than reporting the fraction of all mistakes involving carries.
Split head discovery from head evaluation and correct for searches over layers, heads, prompts, pairs, and thresholds.
Use tokenizer-agnostic position alignment and pin exact model/tokenizer revisions in LLM mechanistic work.
Global weight distance is a weak proxy for functional or circuit continuity; compare activation pathways and intervention effects.
Make arithmetic dataset splits deterministic and publish the indices, especially when only a subset of an exhaustive space is used.
Generate one globally seeded split before distributed sharding; never let ranks independently construct train/test corpora.
State custom positional-encoding deviations explicitly; rotating values is not interchangeable with standard q/k RoPE.
A full-adder analogy is most useful when converted into falsifiable truth-table and interchange-intervention predictions.
Later arithmetic-circuit work should compare human carry algorithms against bag-of-heuristics and alternative representation-level accounts.
open_questions: Does the proposed two-layer circuit remain faithful under mean, resample, activation-patching, and causal-scrubbing interventions?
Can the full model's logits be reconstructed from the proposed digit-sum, decision-head, and carry-MLP subcircuit?
How stable are decision heads and selected neuron sets under dozens of seeds and controlled hyperparameter sweeps?
Would centered PCA, supervised probes on held-out examples, and nonlinear representation tests preserve the claimed layerwise separation?
Does standard query/key-only RoPE learn the same circuit as the repository's query/key/value rotary transform?
Which training dynamics cause the six-digit out-of-distribution staircase to decay after epoch 500?
Can an explicit regularizer stabilize unseen-position routing without any long examples?
What is the minimum and optimal distribution of priming examples across carry-chain length and position?
Why does decoder priming harm three-digit performance, and can replay or multi-width balancing prevent it?
Does fine-tuning preserve individual causal pathways despite the small global norm change?
Can one model generalize jointly across operand length, operand count, base, notation, and overflow?
Does symbol relabeling or reversed digit order reveal a token-position lookup rather than decimal algorithm?
How does the circuit behave on adversarial runs of nines, longest carry chains, and near-overflow examples?
Are the selected MLP neurons necessary and sufficient at the single-example level or only in aggregate?
Do independent held-out prompts reproduce the 7B head rankings and pair-ablation effects?
How much of Llemma and Zephyr arithmetic is explained by carry circuitry versus sparse magnitude heuristics or helical number representations?
Can causal abstraction map toy-model variables to large-model internal states without assuming identical components?
Do current larger base and instruction models use the same motifs across natural language, code, and symbolic arithmetic?
Can exact Boolean or finite-state circuits be extracted and formally verified from the trained small model?
What dataset and intervention suite should operationally distinguish an abstract algorithm from an in-distribution algorithmic motif?
Can a seeded, dependency-locked release reproduce every figure and table from raw results on commodity hardware?

competitive_landscape.title: Investigating the Limitations of Transformers with Simple Arithmetic Tasks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strict arithmetic-transformer predecessor studying extrapolation and surface representation.
competitive_landscape.difference: Nogueira et al. show that formatting and position representations can support very long arithmetic outputs, whereas the target studies a small fixed-format model's internal carry allocation rather than optimizing length extrapolation.

competitive_landscape.title: Thinking Like Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Theoretical predecessor for expressing algorithms as transformer programs.
competitive_landscape.difference: Weiss et al. use RASP to construct and reason about symbolic transformer computations; the target infers a learned decimal circuit from weights and activations without proving RASP-style equivalence.

competitive_landscape.title: The Neural Data Router: Adaptive Control Flow in Transformers Improves Systematic Generalization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Architectural predecessor for systematic generalization on algorithmic tasks.
competitive_landscape.difference: The Neural Data Router modifies control flow to improve systematic extrapolation, while the target diagnoses ordinary transformer circuitry and observes that its zero-shot length transfer fails.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
competitive_landscape.relationship: Training-dynamics predecessor for delayed algorithmic generalization and weight-norm changes.
competitive_landscape.difference: Power et al. establish grokking on modular and algorithmic tasks; the target reports an earlier QK/attention transition in ordinary addition and calls it non-grokking without a formal phase analysis.

competitive_landscape.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
competitive_landscape.relationship: Mechanistic predecessor for abrupt attention-head circuit formation.
competitive_landscape.difference: Olsson et al. document phase changes associated with induction heads across training; this prior weakens broad novelty for the target's visually abrupt QK staircase while addressing a different computation.

competitive_landscape.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest prior mechanistic training study of an addition-like transformer circuit.
competitive_landscape.difference: Nanda et al. identify and causally test a Fourier circuit for modular addition; the target studies ordinary decimal carry routing and MLP correction but provides weaker circuit reconstruction and intervention robustness.

competitive_landscape.title: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Arithmetic Reasoning in Language Models using Causal Mediation Analysis
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strict predecessor for causal localization of arithmetic in pretrained language models.
competitive_landscape.difference: Stolfo et al. use causal mediation to separate early attention transport from later result processing across arithmetic tasks; the target uses visual head scans and zero pair ablations in three 7B fine-tunes after developing a more detailed toy carry hypothesis.

competitive_landscape.title: Randomized Positional Encodings Boost Length Generalization of Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strict positional-encoding predecessor for length generalization.
competitive_landscape.difference: Ruoss et al. randomize positions during training to improve extrapolation; the target uses a fixed custom rotary scheme and longer-example priming, then explains why unprimed OOD positions deteriorate.

competitive_landscape.title: The Impact of Positional Encoding on Length Generalization in Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strict systematic study of position encodings and sequence-length extrapolation.
competitive_landscape.difference: Kazemnejad et al. compare positional schemes across tasks and highlight the importance of architecture/encoding choices; the target contributes circuit observations but does not compare its nonstandard rotary implementation to alternatives.

competitive_landscape.title: Length Generalization in Arithmetic Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct arithmetic length-generalization predecessor cited by the target.
competitive_landscape.difference: Jelassi et al. evaluate addition beyond trained widths and show that a tiny set of longer examples can transform extrapolation; the target reproduces priming behavior and adds an internal analysis showing that the clean fixed-width module allocation changes.

competitive_landscape.title: The Clock and the Pizza: Two Stories in Mechanistic Explanation of Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct cautionary predecessor about algorithm diversity in trained addition networks.
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhong et al. find Clock, Pizza, mixed, and other modular-addition algorithms across seeds and hyperparameters; the target's six-run qualitative consistency and shifting three-layer roles do not exclude comparable diversity.

competitive_landscape.title: Reasoning or Reciting? Exploring the Capabilities and Limitations of Language Models Through Counterfactual Tasks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strict predecessor advocating counterfactual tests of apparent reasoning.
competitive_landscape.difference: Wu et al. alter task rules to distinguish reusable reasoning from familiar-pattern recitation; the target does not test counterfactual bases, symbols, order, or carry rules despite making algorithmic claims.

competitive_landscape.title: Teaching Arithmetic to Small Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct small-transformer arithmetic predecessor.
competitive_landscape.difference: Lee et al. study data format, training phase changes, and length failure in small arithmetic transformers; the target's distinctive addition is a proposed attention/MLP carry decomposition and task-conditioned causal diagnostics.

competitive_landscape.title: Arithmetic with Language Models: from Memorization to Computation
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strict arithmetic-learning predecessor separating internal encoding, computation, and decoding.
competitive_landscape.difference: Maltoni and Ferrara analyze learned arithmetic computation and generalization under alternative encodings; the target focuses more narrowly on decimal carry components and tries to bridge them to fine-tuned 7B models.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Addition in Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest direct pre-v1 paper, reverse-engineering ordinary n-digit addition in a small transformer.
competitive_landscape.difference: Quirke and Barez identify parallel digit streams, local carry predicates, and a bounded-carry failure in a one-layer decoder; the target extends the question to a canonical two-layer encoder allocation, final-MLP carry correction, priming, and suggestive pretrained-LLM evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: What Algorithms can Transformers Learn? A Study in Length Generalization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Near-concurrent framework relating learned algorithms to length extrapolation.
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhou et al. use formal program structure and length generalization to ask which algorithms transformers learn; by that stronger criterion the target's unprimed circuit is a fixed-position motif because its zero-shot longer-width behavior collapses.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Addition and Subtraction in Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest later comprehensive mechanistic successor.
competitive_landscape.difference: Quirke et al. analyze 49 models across addition, subtraction, and mixed operations with stronger systematic ablation and node constraints, greatly broadening and tightening the target's smaller two-layer case study.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later architectural counterexample to weak length extrapolation.
competitive_landscape.difference: McLeish et al. use digit-relative embeddings and related architectural changes to report up to 99% accuracy on 100-digit addition after training on at most 20 digits; the target supplies richer internals but far weaker zero-shot scaling.

competitive_landscape.title: Position Coupling: Improving Length Generalization of Arithmetic Transformers Using Task Structure
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later task-structured position method and theoretical addition baseline.
competitive_landscape.difference: Cho et al. couple corresponding digit positions and extrapolate from lengths up to 30 to tests at 200 digits with a theoretical construction; the target's custom rotary positions fail without priming and have no formal scaling result.

competitive_landscape.title: Physics of Language Models: Part 2.1, Grade-School Math and the Hidden Reasoning Process
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later broad study of language-model grade-school arithmetic and hidden computation.
competitive_landscape.difference: Allen-Zhu and Li investigate data, representation, and hidden reasoning processes at a broader task/model scale; the target offers a more compact component narrative for one addition format but little scaling evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpreting and Improving Large Language Models in Arithmetic Calculation
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later pretrained-LLM arithmetic interpretation and intervention work.
competitive_landscape.difference: This work pairs mechanistic analysis with methods intended to improve calculation, while the target's 7B section is a small same-sample head search and does not demonstrate a complete or improving intervention.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpreting Arithmetic Mechanism in Large Language Models through Comparative Neuron Analysis
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later neuron-level arithmetic mechanism study in large models.
competitive_landscape.difference: The comparative-neuron approach searches for arithmetic-selective internal units across conditions, providing a different localization route from the target's broad small-model MLP partition and attention-pair ablations.

competitive_landscape.title: Algorithmic Capabilities of Random Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later control on how much algorithmic structure architecture supplies before learning.
competitive_landscape.difference: Random-transformer results caution that decodable algorithmic features or useful routing geometry need not uniquely identify a learned human algorithm; the target does not include untrained or label-randomized circuit controls.

competitive_landscape.title: Arithmetic Transformers Can Length-Generalize in Both Operand Length and Count
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later stronger multi-axis arithmetic extrapolation result.
competitive_landscape.difference: This work targets both operand length and number of operands, broadening the generalization criterion beyond the target's three-to-six-digit two-operand setup and showing that architecture/data design can overcome its failure mode.

competitive_landscape.title: Arithmetic Without Algorithms: Language Models Solve Math With a Bag of Heuristics
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later direct competing account of arithmetic computation in pretrained language models.
competitive_landscape.difference: Nikankin et al. causally identify sparse operand-range and answer heuristics across LLMs and argue that their combination explains arithmetic behavior; this directly cautions against inferring the toy model's clean human carry algorithm from staircase heads in three 7B models.

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models Use Trigonometry to Do Addition
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later competing representation-level and causal account of addition in LLMs.
competitive_landscape.difference: Kantamneni and Tegmark identify generalized helical number representations and a Clock-style addition mechanism across mid-sized models; this is a more explicit alternative to the target's qualitative residual similarity and attention-head story.

competitive_landscape.title: Arithmetic in the Wild: Llama uses Base-10 Addition to Reason About Cyclic Concepts
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current successor connecting arithmetic representations to non-arithmetic cyclic reasoning.
competitive_landscape.difference: This work tests a broader causal abstraction of base-10 addition inside Llama on cyclic concepts, moving beyond the target's one-format four-digit prompts and visually analogous residual states.

competitive_landscape.title: Are Arithmetic Heuristic Neurons Form-Invariant? A Mechanistic Analysis of Symbols, Text, and Code in LLMs
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current cross-format causal successor for arithmetic mechanisms.
competitive_landscape.difference: Naganna et al. test necessity, sufficiency, and activation transfer for neurons shared across symbolic arithmetic, word problems, and code in Llama-3 models; this directly addresses the format restriction and weak causal validation of the target's 7B section.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims that two-layer transformers implement the ordinary carrying-over algorithm modularly, with local digit addition in the first layer, carry decisions in second-layer attention, and carried-one application in the final MLP; that this allocation is robust across hyperparameters, depth, decoder models, and longer lengths; and that related circuitry is visible in three 7B language models.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Strict predecessors cover small-transformer arithmetic, grokking and abrupt circuit formation, causal arithmetic mediation in pretrained models, positional encoding and length extrapolation, counterfactual reasoning tests, and ordinary n-digit addition circuits. The closest direct predecessor, arXiv:2310.13121, already reverse-engineers position-specific digit streams and carry behavior in a one-layer addition transformer. The target's real addition is the two-layer attention/MLP division of decimal carry, a useful plus/minus-one ablation diagnostic, variants across encoder/decoder and one-to-three layers, a four-digit case, internal analysis of priming/fine-tuning, and a tentative toy-to-7B comparison. Its strongest broad claims are narrowed by failed zero-shot length transfer, redistributed primed computation, broad neuron sets, off-manifold ablations, uncentered post-hoc projections, and same-sample LLM head search. Later work supplies larger model families, stronger causal circuits, much better length generalization, and alternative bag-of-heuristics or helical accounts.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Novelty is moderate for the narrow controlled two-layer carry decomposition, low for arithmetic-transformer and phase-transition framing, and low-to-moderate for the pretrained-LLM extension. The most defensible conclusion is that a recurring fixed-format algorithmic motif can divide direct sums, carry routing, and correction across transformer components. The paper does not establish a unique abstract addition algorithm, universal module allocation, length-invariant implementation, sparse neuron circuit, or faithful carry mechanism in 7B LLMs.

reviewer_notes: Primary-source review completed 2026-08-23 against arXiv v2 (submitted 2024-01-15, revised 2024-01-17). Every extracted page was read (41/41), every page was rendered and visually inspected, and all 26 numbered figures/graphics and five tables were audited, including learning curves, attention maps, residual projections, length-generalization panels, and the full-adder schematic. The official source bundle (SHA-256 22697527cc69776bb42d7c58dd4e6b024cdfa4bcb93a850244f7b756e3f82fec) was audited across all 49 files and all 44 supplied one-page graphics: 29/29 referenced assets and 15/15 unused revision assets opened, and a clean build reproduced 41 pages with no undefined citations or references. The manuscript-official repository was audited at exact commit 977cc016e36fce067d1b82ef2e269ebddce6324d, which is 13 days later than arXiv v2 and adds decoder helpers absent from the contemporaneous tree. All ten Python files passed static compilation, all six notebooks parsed as JSON, and the shipped encoder checkpoint loaded into current model.py for a finite CPU dummy forward; no expensive GPU training or inference was run. Competitive priority was checked from official primary records through 2026-08-23; 16 listed works predate or are effectively concurrent with v1 and 12 are later/current comparators. Quantitative findings are author-reported unless labeled contradiction-audit or reviewer-inference. The main material contradictions are failed zero-shot length transfer versus abstract-algorithm language, redistributed carry computation after successful priming, broad rather than sparse neuron localization, uncentered code projections described as PCA, nonstandard value rotation omitted from the architecture description, circular LLM head selection/evaluation, inconsistent four-digit task/threshold captions, a guaranteed length-trainer crash, absent fine-tuning code, incompatible current-versus-shipped data formats, and invalid per-rank corpus construction.
